title: Se with a verb: books banned, teachers dismissed

sections.content: You know *se* with a verb from B1 Unit 6. It lets you say what was done without saying who did it. With a noun, the verb agrees with it (*se prohibían libros*). With no noun, the verb stays singular (*se prohibía hablar*). Here is a case that mixes both: people. They take the personal *a* (you know it from A1 Unit 24), and the verb stays singular: *se vigilaba a los periodistas*. This suits a topic where the doers are the state, the police or the army and you want to focus on what happened.

items.spanish: Se prohibían libros, películas y canciones.
items.english: Books, films and songs were banned.

sections.content: Compare *Los periodistas eran vigilados por la policía* (passive with *ser*, from Lesson 1) with *Se vigilaba a los periodistas*: the second leaves the doer out completely. Check the noun: things make the verb plural (*se quemaron libros*), people with *a* do not (*se despidió a muchos profesores*).
